Kokonut/VST Pedal

Concept Hardware · No prototype yet

Off the desk.
On the floor.

A concept for a stompbox that runs your Windows VST plug-ins, so the sound you dialled in at the desk comes to the gig without a laptop.

Turn a knob · Stomp the switch · Drag to look around

Synthesised live in your browser with the Web Audio API. A sketch of the feel, not a VST host. Yet.

The question

Why should your sound
stay at home?

A DAW puts a world of amps, pedals and spaces a click away. Getting those exact sounds onto a stage usually means bringing the computer too: a laptop on an ironing board, an audio interface, a nervous glance at the battery.

The idea is simple to say and hard to build: a pedal that hosts your Windows VST plug-ins itself. One box on the floor, your signal chain inside, real knobs and a footswitch in charge.

This is an early concept. Hardware, plug-in compatibility, latency, controls and release plans are all still open. Nothing here is a product specification.

Signal path

Simple on the outside.

  1. Guitar
  2. Input
  3. Your VST chain
  4. Output
  5. Amp / PA

Open questions

The hard parts,
on purpose.

A concept is only useful if it’s honest about what could stop it.

Latency

A guitarist feels delay long before they hear it. The whole chain needs a latency budget measured in single-digit milliseconds.

Hosting

Running Windows plug-ins means running Windows, or something compatible, inside a pedal. That shapes the processor, cooling and power.

Plug-in licensing

Many plug-ins are activated per machine or online. The pedal has to respect that without becoming a chore.

Stage-proof

Boots fast, survives a kick, reads in the dark and never needs a mouse. A stage is not a studio.

Roadmap

Where it’s headed.

A direction, not a promise. No dates until the feasibility work says yes.

  1. 01Now

    Concept

  2. 02

  3. 03

  4. 04

    On stage

    Field testing with players in real rigs.
